summary: Build the SPEED-TAX GATE: a committed, reusable paired measurement (native E5 spine vs tree arms at matched shape/flags) emitting measured per-forward ratio (decode_seconds/spec_drafts basis - NO TPS/accept hand-rolls), accept/event, and traffic predicted-vs-measured - PLUS a tree-size/shape SWEEP mode (chain-5 / caterpillar-9 / wider-deeper) to measure how the tax SCALES with node count (the replay route claims state-cost invariant to N; legacy is linear-in-N). CPU build + reduce-existing-artifacts now; GPU sweep deferred.

backfill.scaling_signal: n=2 distinct N values at the legacy route = DIRECTION ONLY, not shape. (1) Legacy tax GROWS with N: chain5(N=5) 0.3517 -> cat9(N=9) 0.3936/0.3936/0.3976 s/fwd (+0.042-0.046; ratio 1.653x -> 1.850-1.869x); the three N=9 arms agree within 1% across three separate boots/campaigns, so the step is real, not boot noise. Both shapes are depth-5, so the added 4 nodes are width. [F] OLS over the 4 legacy points: slope 0.0108 s/fwd per draft node (95% CI [0.0095,0.0121], small-n indicative), preferred over N-invariant by dof-adjusted MSE — labeled FIT, and with 2 x-values any monotone curve fits. (2) Magnitude vs model: the w78aq6xum row model (3N+2a+1) predicts only +6.3ms floor step N=5->9; measured is +42-46ms ~= 7x the row-traffic floor slope — the marginal node cost is NOT GDN state-row traffic alone; candidates (undecomposable at n=2): the n_pad 8->16 step (a built-in confound of exactly these two points), verifier mask/sampler work, drafter rollout width. (3) Replay: ONE point at ONE N — 0.3270 s/fwd (1.537x) at N=9, sitting BELOW legacy at N=5 (0.3517); directionally consistent with the N-invariance claim (rows=2+a) but it is a single accept-bug-confounded point, so no invariance test exists (fit correctly reports INSUFFICIENT_POINTS/preferred=None). The GPU sweep (N=5/9/12/13/15 under the N_PAD=16 cap, x{legacy,replay}+same-campaign native, matrix banked at output/fr13_speed_tax_gate/sweep/sweep_commands.sh) is what discriminates within-pad legacy slope vs 3N+2a+1, replay flatness, and width(cat12_w3_d5) vs depth(cat13_d6); run it AFTER the replay live accept-bug fix (replay arms need unmerged fr13-replay-route@9d4d22e3).

overreaches: traffic_model has no batch-size term: w78aq6xum's GB/forward accounting in FR13_DIRECTION_AND_NUMBERS.md is B=4-scaled state-only, while the gate emits per-request (B=1) weights+state. Constants are exact and all backfill/sweep arms are B=1 so no emitted [P] cell is wrong, but reusing the function unmodified at the B=4 final-gate regime would understate state traffic ~4x; it should take B as an input.

pairing_check mechanically enforces only the battery fields + BATCH_INVARIANT; other launcher flag-state (conv-fix ON/OFF, replay-campaign boot1 code state across the three cat9 arms) is not compared and is carried as caveat labels instead. 'Mismatches labeled' holds, but the doc's pairing-rule phrase 'same flag-state' overstates what is enforced vs labeled.
'All three N=9 arms agree within 1%' is rounding-level optimistic: max/min spread is 1.02% (it is +/-0.51% of the mean, which the doc states correctly elsewhere).

replay_cat9_b2's BI=1 rests on run_header prose ('other_env: same as boot1') supplied via the --flags override rather than an explicitly recorded per-boot flag; this is labeled on the arm, in the doc, and in the ladder row (and the BACKFILL itself flags it), but it remains documentation-inferred, not artifact-recorded.

The FR13_LADDER_LOG.md entry does not contain the literal 'FR13-TAX' row prefix (the 6 verbatim FR13-TAX rows live only in FR13_SPEED_TAX_BASELINE.md); the bind claim's wording is accurate ('ladder entry'), but the grep handle differs from the row format — cosmetic.

OLS slope CI [0.0095,0.0121] is mechanically produced by 3 near-identical replicates at N=9 plus one N=5 point (dof=2); the direction-only and 'any monotone curve fits 2 x-values' hedges cover this, but the CI should not be quoted without those hedges attached.
